overview: The Medford School Committee approved the scope of a major HVAC replacement project for the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools, updated facilities and pool rental rate cards, and passed a resolution restricting future purchases of fossil-fuel building equipment. The committee also referred matters concerning capital planning, curriculum assessment reviews, and the potential co-location of the Curtis-Tufts School to subcommittees.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee convened in executive session to discuss strategy regarding collective bargaining preparations with multiple staff unions.

items.title: Consent Agenda and Routine Approvals
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes, bills, payrolls, a $1,000 donation to the string ensemble, and high school travel to Puerto Rico.

items.title: Superintendent's Updates and Comments
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent reported on high school Ethics Bowl achievements, Child Abuse Prevention Month, upcoming school orientations, and the schedule for the FY25 budget hearing.

items.title: Fine and Performing Arts Updates
items.summary: Coordinators Suzanne Fee and Haley Rello presented updates on visual arts grants and classes, upcoming district Arts Month events, and student awards, including a state gold medal for the high school orchestra.

items.title: Motion to Table Resolution on Fossil Fuel Building Equipment
items.summary: Following debate over building authority and procedural order, the committee voted to table a resolution banning fossil-fuel powered equipment purchases until after the HVAC technical presentation.

items.title: HVAC Assessment and Scope Approval
items.summary: Staff and consultants detailed building assessments showing failing HVAC systems at the Andrews and McGlynn schools, explored electrical and geothermal constraints, and the committee approved the proposed partial-decarbonization scope of work estimated at $15 to $20 million.

items.title: Suspension and Discipline Report
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent presented suspension and referral data from August 2023 through March 2024, noting 61 out-of-school suspensions, demographic trends, and district interventions.

items.title: Rate Card Adjustments
items.summary: Approved a 10 percent increase on school facility rental fees and an increase to pool usage fees to address operating shortfalls.

items.title: MASC/MASS Conference Delegate Nominations
items.summary: Appointed Member Ruseau as the voting delegate and Member Olapade as alternate delegate for the annual joint conference assembly.

items.title: Capital Needs Assessment Review Resolution
items.summary: Approved a resolution referring the district's capital needs assessment and planning document to the Strategic and Capital Planning Subcommittee for review by June 10, 2024.

items.title: Curtis-Tufts Co-Location Study Resolution
items.summary: Referred the question of co-locating the Curtis-Tufts alternative program on the Medford High School campus to the Special Education and Behavioral Health Subcommittee for stakeholder input and a report back by June 3, 2024.

items.title: Curriculum and Assessment Review Resolution
items.summary: Approved a resolution directing the Subcommittee on Curriculum, Instruction, Assessment and Accountability to meet with staff to establish protocols and timelines for evaluating newly adopted curricula.

items.title: Resolution on the End of Fossil Fuel Building Equipment Purchases
items.summary: Removed from the table and approved a resolution prohibiting the purchase of replacement or new fossil-fuel powered facility equipment without explicit School Committee authorization.
